newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares seen recovering on upbeat U.S..
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares seen recovering on upbeat U.S..

text.p: Share prices were recovering in early trading in Singapore on Wednesday on upbeat news from the U.S., dealers said.
"Singapore should be taking its lead from the U.S," one local dealer said.
Firm growth expectations from U.S. computer companies IBM, Hewlett-Packard and Intel, together with good consumer confidence should have a positive effect on Singapore share prices, dealers agreed.
"The sentiment and euphoria may rub off some more on the Singapore stock exchange," one dealer said.
Singapore's Straits Times Industrials Index was up 9.43 points at 2,179.61 at 0225 GMT on volume of 47.07 million units.

Volume was high in sporting goods firm Ossia International, on its first day of trading after its initial public offering. Its price rose to Singapore 70.5 cents on volume of 20.26 million at 0225 GMT. The offer price was 61 cents.

Shares in computer company Aztech Systems resumed trading in the morning and were down two cents on volume of 1.22 million units. Aztech has said it may pay only modest damages from its copyright dispute with rival company Creative Technology Ltd.
